newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast light crudes edge up with April WTI.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast light crudes edge up with April WTI.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crude edged up Wednesday with April WTI/Cushing, but differentials held steady as traders moved to the sidelines to evaluate the new month.
Buyers last indicated they would buy March barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) at $1.60 off April WTI.
The grade's major seller appeared to be close to selling a March cargo late Tuesday, but had not closed the deal early Wednesday.
Outright prices stood at $19.80/20.00 a barrel, up five cents from Tuesday.
Arco late Tuesday said it would limit shipments on its California Line 63 pipeline for the first time in three months.
Space was restricted to 98.1 percent of shippers' nominations, as several heavy crude shippers were seen pouring extra crude into the line to alleviate backed-up supply, traders said.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with some sellers claiming the price could rise if more of the diluent grade was needed to push heavy crudes along the line.
Kern River heavy crude stayed steady after falling two days ago, with prices talked 13.84/14.04 a barrel, traders said.
Chevron said the number four crude unit at its El Segundo plant returned to service recently, only a few days after its scheduled return.
The unit had forced more crude into the market, traders said.
